pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- Converts destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent to be an array.
- Patches and fixes so every sentence of code that was using evet.destinationCalendar can support the new type of array.
- The logic here is to fallback to normal behaviour has having one main destinationCalendar but also supports multiple so host can get invited correctly.

Fixes #7754 
## Loom 
Creating event and rescheduling:
https://www.loom.com/share/3cb3af513d274ed2bdfed44e48edddf6?sid=d81ce3de-2893-4a30-b085-ff67c31b7dfb

Canceling event:
https://www.loom.com/share/7ef505d4665e4d4982d2bb2d7b118085?sid=cd43c97c-aa86-4667-979f-f6492adf3365

## Requirement/Documentation

## Type of change

<!-- Please delete bullets that are not relevant. -->

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

- Are there environment variables that should be set? No
- What are the minimal test data to have? Setup a collective event using teampro and teamfree users. Add any app calendar to those accounts and add them as host for collective event.
- What is expected (happy path) to have (input and output)? Collective event with 2 host and every user with any calendar app installed should receive proper calendar events.
- Any other important info that could help to test that PR

## Mandatory Tasks

- [X] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

raw_findings.body: The find() compares every destinationCalendar entry's externalId against the same falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches a real externalId, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the Google Calendar API update call receives an undefined calendarId, failing the update
raw_findings.failure_mode: Calendar update requests are sent with an undefined calendarId, causing the update to fail or target the wrong calendar
raw_findings.impact: The find() compares every destinationCalendar entry's externalId against the same falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches a real externalId, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the Google Calendar API update call receives an undefined calendarId, failing the update
raw_findings.root_cause: When converting to an array, the lookup key used for the fallback branch was mistakenly set to the same falsy externalCalendarId that caused the branch to execute
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Select the destination calendar using a valid key (e.g. credentialId) instead of matching externalId against the already-known falsy externalCalendarId, e.g. fall back to event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId
raw_findings.title: updateEvent calendarId lookup can never match, always resolving to undefined
raw_findings.trigger: updateEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId (falsy), causing this fallback branch to execute

raw_findings.body: find() never matches because it's comparing every destinationCalendar entry's externalId to the same falsy externalCalendarId, so calendarId resolves to undefined and the delete falls back to the 'primary' calendar instead of the intended host destination calendar, deleting from the wrong calendar
raw_findings.failure_mode: Events are deleted from the default 'primary' calendar rather than the correct destination calendar, leaving stale events behind
raw_findings.impact: find() never matches because it's comparing every destinationCalendar entry's externalId to the same falsy externalCalendarId, so calendarId resolves to undefined and the delete falls back to the 'primary' calendar instead of the intended host destination calendar, deleting from the wrong calendar
raw_findings.root_cause: Same erroneous self-referential find introduced while converting destinationCalendar to an array
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Look up the entry with a proper identifier (credentialId) or fall back to the first destinationCalendar entry's externalId, e.g. event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId
raw_findings.title: deleteEvent calendarId lookup silently falls back to primary calendar due to self-referential comparison
raw_findings.trigger: deleteEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId for a host whose destination calendar externalId is not equal to that falsy value

raw_findings.body: credentialId is unconditionally set to undefined for non-calendar (video) results instead of falling back to result.credentialId as before, losing the credential reference needed for later video event updates/cancellations
raw_findings.failure_mode: Booking reference for the video credential is stored without credentialId, breaking future video-event update/delete lookups that rely on it
raw_findings.impact: credentialId is unconditionally set to undefined for non-calendar (video) results instead of falling back to result.credentialId as before, losing the credential reference needed for later video event updates/cancellations
raw_findings.root_cause: While removing the now-invalid evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId array access, the legitimate result.credentialId fallback for the non-calendar branch was also removed
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep result.credentialId regardless of isCalendarType, e.g. credentialId: result.credentialId
raw_findings.title: credentialId dropped for video event references in EventManager.create
raw_findings.trigger: A dedicated video meeting is created as part of booking creation (isCalendarType is false for the video result)

raw_findings.body: The optional-chained push becomes a no-op on null, so team members' collected destinationCalendars are discarded and their calendars never receive the created event, defeating the multi-host purpose of this PR
raw_findings.failure_mode: Collective-event hosts other than the organizer do not get the event created in their destination calendars whenever the organizer has none configured
raw_findings.impact: The optional-chained push becomes a no-op on null, so team members' collected destinationCalendars are discarded and their calendars never receive the created event, defeating the multi-host purpose of this PR
raw_findings.root_cause: evt.destinationCalendar can be null and Array.prototype.push is invoked via optional chaining, which silently no-ops instead of creating a new array
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assign a fresh array instead of relying on push through optional chaining, e.g. evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];
raw_findings.title: Team members' destinationCalendars silently dropped when organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar
raw_findings.trigger: Collective event booking where neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar is set, so evt.destinationCalendar is null

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the organization: { select: { slug: true } } clause in the dynamic-user prisma.user.findMany select block
raw_findings.title: organization.slug selection removed from dynamic-booking user query
raw_findings.trigger: Dynamic booking flow (!eventTypeId) loading users via prisma.user.findMany inside loadUsers

raw_findings.body: For every non-Google calendar provider, the newly introduced per-credential/per-host destinationCalendar selection has no effect: the extra credentialId argument is silently discarded, so collective events with multiple hosts on those providers keep being created against the wrong or first destination calendar instead of each host's own calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Interface widening silently degrades into a no-op for most concrete implementations, so review/tests based only on the interface will miss that the feature only works for Google Calendar.
raw_findings.impact: For every non-Google calendar provider, the newly introduced per-credential/per-host destinationCalendar selection has no effect: the extra credentialId argument is silently discarded, so collective events with multiple hosts on those providers keep being created against the wrong or first destination calendar instead of each host's own calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The Calendar interface's createEvent signature was widened to add a mandatory credentialId parameter without a corresponding contract/mechanism ensuring all implementations consume it for destination-calendar resolution.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either update every Calendar implementation to accept and use credentialId to pick the matching destinationCalendar entry, or make the parameter optional (credentialId?: number) and document that implementations must opt in to honor it.
raw_findings.title: createEvent interface now requires credentialId that most Calendar implementations ignore
raw_findings.trigger: EventManager/CalendarManager now always calls calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id) for every Calendar implementation (basecamp3, closecom, exchange2013calendar, exchange2016calendar, exchangecalendar, hubspot, larkcalendar, office365calendar, salesforce, sendgrid, zoho-bigin, zohocrm), but these implementations still declare createEvent(event: CalendarEvent) and never read the credentialId argument.

raw_findings.body: Using two different names (externalId vs. externalCalendarId) for the same external-calendar-id concept within the same file increases the chance of wiring mistakes when mapping between these closely related interfaces.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Naming drift within a single type-definition file makes cross-referencing related interfaces error-prone for future maintainers.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the newly added field to externalCalendarId to match the existing convention already used by PartialReference in the same file.

finding.impact: Using two different names (externalId vs. externalCalendarId) for the same external-calendar-id concept within the same file increases the chance of wiring mistakes when mapping between these closely related interfaces.
finding.root_cause: The new field was named without reconciling it with the pre-existing externalCalendarId naming convention used elsewhere in the same file for the identical concept.
finding.suggested_fix: Rename the newly added field to externalCalendarId to match the existing convention already used by PartialReference in the same file.
finding.title: Inconsistent naming between EventResult.externalId and PartialReference.externalCalendarId
finding.trigger: A maintainer reads EventManager.d.ts and maps EventResult fields to PartialReference fields (as EventManager.ts already does via `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined`).
finding.verifier_reason: Candidate is explicitly categorized as 'style' and describes naming inconsistency, not a functional defect. Stylistic findings should be dropped per instructions.

rejected_findings.reason: Candidate is explicitly categorized as 'style' and describes naming inconsistency, not a functional defect. Stylistic findings should be dropped per instructions.

validated_findings.body: Destructuring an empty array leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar as undefined, and accessing .integration on it throws an uncaught TypeError, crashing EventManager.create() and the whole booking-creation flow
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled runtime exception aborts booking creation for any event using the Google Meet fallback logic without a destination calendar
validated_findings.impact: Destructuring an empty array leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar as undefined, and accessing .integration on it throws an uncaught TypeError, crashing EventManager.create() and the whole booking-creation flow
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor destructures the first element of the (possibly empty) destinationCalendar array but omits the optional chaining the previous single-object code relied on
validated_findings.title: Unsafe access to destinationCalendar array element causes TypeError when no calendar is set
validated_findings.trigger: A booking whose evt.destinationCalendar is null/undefined/empty (e.g. no eventType or organizer destinationCalendar configured) uses MeetLocationType as the location
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 119 exists verbatim in patch. Destructuring empty array yields undefined, then accessing .integration without optional chaining throws TypeError. Trigger is realistic: no destinationCalendar configured + MeetLocationType location.

validated_findings.body: The find() compares every destinationCalendar entry's externalId against the same falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches a real externalId, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the Google Calendar API update call receives an undefined calendarId, failing the update
validated_findings.failure_mode: Calendar update requests are sent with an undefined calendarId, causing the update to fail or target the wrong calendar
validated_findings.impact: The find() compares every destinationCalendar entry's externalId against the same falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches a real externalId, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the Google Calendar API update call receives an undefined calendarId, failing the update
validated_findings.root_cause: When converting to an array, the lookup key used for the fallback branch was mistakenly set to the same falsy externalCalendarId that caused the branch to execute
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Select the destination calendar using a valid key (e.g. credentialId) instead of matching externalId against the already-known falsy externalCalendarId, e.g. fall back to event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId
validated_findings.title: updateEvent calendarId lookup can never match, always resolving to undefined
validated_findings.trigger: updateEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId (falsy), causing this fallback branch to execute
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 256 exists verbatim. When externalCalendarId is falsy, the else branch executes find() comparing cal.externalId against the same falsy externalCalendarId, which never matches any real externalId, so selectedCalendar is always undefined.

validated_findings.body: find() never matches because it's comparing every destinationCalendar entry's externalId to the same falsy externalCalendarId, so calendarId resolves to undefined and the delete falls back to the 'primary' calendar instead of the intended host destination calendar, deleting from the wrong calendar
validated_findings.failure_mode: Events are deleted from the default 'primary' calendar rather than the correct destination calendar, leaving stale events behind
validated_findings.impact: find() never matches because it's comparing every destinationCalendar entry's externalId to the same falsy externalCalendarId, so calendarId resolves to undefined and the delete falls back to the 'primary' calendar instead of the intended host destination calendar, deleting from the wrong calendar
validated_findings.root_cause: Same erroneous self-referential find introduced while converting destinationCalendar to an array
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Look up the entry with a proper identifier (credentialId) or fall back to the first destinationCalendar entry's externalId, e.g. event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId
validated_findings.title: deleteEvent calendarId lookup silently falls back to primary calendar due to self-referential comparison
validated_findings.trigger: deleteEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId for a host whose destination calendar externalId is not equal to that falsy value
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 315-317 exist verbatim. Same self-referential find bug as candidate 1 in deleteEvent. Same root cause and fix pattern, but different method - however both are independently fixable sites of the same causal pattern.

validated_findings.body: credentialId is unconditionally set to undefined for non-calendar (video) results instead of falling back to result.credentialId as before, losing the credential reference needed for later video event updates/cancellations
validated_findings.failure_mode: Booking reference for the video credential is stored without credentialId, breaking future video-event update/delete lookups that rely on it
validated_findings.impact: credentialId is unconditionally set to undefined for non-calendar (video) results instead of falling back to result.credentialId as before, losing the credential reference needed for later video event updates/cancellations
validated_findings.root_cause: While removing the now-invalid evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId array access, the legitimate result.credentialId fallback for the non-calendar branch was also removed
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Keep result.credentialId regardless of isCalendarType, e.g. credentialId: result.credentialId
validated_findings.title: credentialId dropped for video event references in EventManager.create
validated_findings.trigger: A dedicated video meeting is created as part of booking creation (isCalendarType is false for the video result)
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 170 exists verbatim. Patch changes from result.credentialId fallback for non-calendar to unconditional undefined. Video results lose credentialId needed for later updates/deletes.

validated_findings.body: The optional-chained push becomes a no-op on null, so team members' collected destinationCalendars are discarded and their calendars never receive the created event, defeating the multi-host purpose of this PR
validated_findings.failure_mode: Collective-event hosts other than the organizer do not get the event created in their destination calendars whenever the organizer has none configured
validated_findings.impact: The optional-chained push becomes a no-op on null, so team members' collected destinationCalendars are discarded and their calendars never receive the created event, defeating the multi-host purpose of this PR
validated_findings.root_cause: evt.destinationCalendar can be null and Array.prototype.push is invoked via optional chaining, which silently no-ops instead of creating a new array
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Assign a fresh array instead of relying on push through optional chaining, e.g. evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];
validated_findings.title: Team members' destinationCalendars silently dropped when organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar
validated_findings.trigger: Collective event booking where neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar is set, so evt.destinationCalendar is null
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1078 exists verbatim. When evt.destinationCalendar is null (neither eventType nor organizer has one), optional chaining makes push a no-op, silently discarding teamDestinationCalendars.

validated_findings.body: user.organization.slug is no longer selected for dynamically-loaded users, so any downstream logic relying on the user's organization slug (e.g. org-scoped booker URLs) receives undefined for these users
validated_findings.failure_mode: Loss of organization slug data causes incorrect or missing organization-aware behavior for dynamically-booked users
validated_findings.impact: user.organization.slug is no longer selected for dynamically-loaded users, so any downstream logic relying on the user's organization slug (e.g. org-scoped booker URLs) receives undefined for these users
validated_findings.root_cause: The loadUsers refactor dropped the organization.slug select clause when restructuring the dynamic-user branch
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the organization: { select: { slug: true } } clause in the dynamic-user prisma.user.findMany select block
validated_findings.title: organization.slug selection removed from dynamic-booking user query
validated_findings.trigger: Dynamic booking flow (!eventTypeId) loading users via prisma.user.findMany inside loadUsers
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Candidate cites LEFT side line 737 claiming organization.slug was removed. Patch shows the select clause was restructured but the evidence doesn't prove organization.slug is missing from the new code - the patch context shows refactoring, not removal of the field.

validated_findings.body: mainHostDestinationCalendar always resolves to the first array entry regardless of which credentialId invoked createEvent, so the organizer attendee's email/externalId in the Google Calendar payload may reference a different host's calendar than the one actually being written to
validated_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect calendar/email metadata is attached to the organizer attendee entry for hosts other than the first destinationCalendar array element
validated_findings.impact: mainHostDestinationCalendar always resolves to the first array entry regardless of which credentialId invoked createEvent, so the organizer attendee's email/externalId in the Google Calendar payload may reference a different host's calendar than the one actually being written to
validated_findings.root_cause: The newly added credentialId parameter is used to pick the calendarId for the API call but not reused to pick the matching destinationCalendar entry for the attendee email field
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute mainHostDestinationCalendar the same way selectedCalendar is computed: calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)
validated_findings.title: Organizer attendee email derived from wrong destinationCalendar entry, ignoring the current credentialId
validated_findings.trigger: A collective event with multiple hosts, each with their own destinationCalendar, where createEvent is invoked once per host via credentialId
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 122 exists but claim is speculative. mainHostDestinationCalendar is derived from first array element, but createEvent receives credentialId and uses it to find selectedCalendar (line 147-149). The email field uses first entry which may be intentional for organizer display. Impact is uncertain without proof of incorrect behavior.

validated_findings.body: Previously slug was set directly on the organization only when billing was disabled (free orgs get an immediate slug, billed orgs wait for approval via requestedSlug in metadata). The flipped condition now sets slug directly only when billing IS enabled and omits it when disabled, bypassing the intended slug-approval flow for billed orgs and leaving free orgs without a slug
validated_findings.failure_mode: Organizations are created with incorrect slug assignment: billed orgs skip the required approval process while free orgs are created without a slug
validated_findings.impact: Previously slug was set directly on the organization only when billing was disabled (free orgs get an immediate slug, billed orgs wait for approval via requestedSlug in metadata). The flipped condition now sets slug directly only when billing IS enabled and omits it when disabled, bypassing the intended slug-approval flow for billed orgs and leaving free orgs without a slug
validated_findings.root_cause: The boolean condition was inverted while converting the `&&` short-circuit expression to a ternary form
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Revert to the original condition: ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })
validated_findings.title: Inverted condition sets organization slug only when team billing is enabled
validated_findings.trigger: Creating an organization, with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED either true or false
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 151 exists verbatim. Original was !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }, new is IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}. Logic is inverted: now sets slug when billing enabled (should wait for approval) and omits when disabled (should set immediately).

validated_findings.body: For every non-Google calendar provider, the newly introduced per-credential/per-host destinationCalendar selection has no effect: the extra credentialId argument is silently discarded, so collective events with multiple hosts on those providers keep being created against the wrong or first destination calendar instead of each host's own calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Interface widening silently degrades into a no-op for most concrete implementations, so review/tests based only on the interface will miss that the feature only works for Google Calendar.
validated_findings.impact: For every non-Google calendar provider, the newly introduced per-credential/per-host destinationCalendar selection has no effect: the extra credentialId argument is silently discarded, so collective events with multiple hosts on those providers keep being created against the wrong or first destination calendar instead of each host's own calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: The Calendar interface's createEvent signature was widened to add a mandatory credentialId parameter without a corresponding contract/mechanism ensuring all implementations consume it for destination-calendar resolution.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Either update every Calendar implementation to accept and use credentialId to pick the matching destinationCalendar entry, or make the parameter optional (credentialId?: number) and document that implementations must opt in to honor it.
validated_findings.title: createEvent interface now requires credentialId that most Calendar implementations ignore
validated_findings.trigger: EventManager/CalendarManager now always calls calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id) for every Calendar implementation (basecamp3, closecom, exchange2013calendar, exchange2016calendar, exchangecalendar, hubspot, larkcalendar, office365calendar, salesforce, sendgrid, zoho-bigin, zohocrm), but these implementations still declare createEvent(event: CalendarEvent) and never read the credentialId argument.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 221 exists but claim is about interface widening without implementation updates. This is a design concern, not a concrete bug. The implementations may work correctly by ignoring the extra parameter (JS allows this). No proven runtime failure.
